title: Migrate review-report plugin to contract v2
goal: Adopt the v2 result contract (result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason), fix the bare extract_first_json_object lens parse defect, inject router budget guidance into lens prompts, and declare router budgets in the manifest — all within the review-report plugin boundary.

steps.description: Write failing tests (SPEC assertions) for all acceptance criteria before touching any implementation: (a) v2 result written on every exit path with result_contract/verdict/disposition/reason; (b) valid_verdicts enforced — each emittable verdict is in the declared set; (c) each lens prompt contains a budget-guidance block sourced from _route_resolve_max_turns/_route_resolve_timeout; (d) disposition:exhausted emitted when the router signals budget exhaustion; (e) _rr_parse_lens_out recovers via schema-gate rather than LAST-wins bare extract; (f) manifest declares result_contract:2 and router: block. Run the new SPECs and confirm each fails for the stated reason.

Amend manifest.yaml: (1) add `result_contract: 2` under the provides: block; (2) add a `config.router:` section with `timeout_s` and `max_turns` drawn from the same ranges the engine enforces (timeout_s: 300, max_turns: 25 as defaults matching the lenses' T2 budget — template override still wins per manifest-router-budget.sh). The primary:true output already exists; record that in the plan notes. Run SPEC-f to confirm it now passes.

Add `_rr_lens_envelope_schema_ok` predicate and route lenses.sh _rr_parse_lens_out through `_llm_envelope_parse --schema-gate _rr_lens_envelope_schema_ok`, mirroring the security-lens pattern (security-lens/plugin.sh:42 and :140). Source scripts/lib/llm-agent.sh in plugin.sh (before lenses.sh is sourced). Keep identical visible-failure behaviour: emit review_report.lens.unparseable and degrade to empty findings when the schema gate fails. Run SPEC-e to confirm the recovery test now passes.

Add `_rr_budget_guidance <max_turns> <timeout_s>` helper to plugin.sh, mirroring `_design_budget_guidance` from plugins/agent/design/plugin.sh:64-90. Resolve values via `_route_resolve_max_turns` and `_route_resolve_timeout` in `_rr_run_inner` and inject the block into `_rr_build_lens_prompt` (or prepend it per-lens before writing the prompt file in _rr_fanout_lenses). Never hand-copy numbers — always call the router helpers so the block drifts with the enforced limit. Run SPEC-c and SPEC-d to confirm budget guidance and exhausted disposition pass.

Write v2 result file on every terminal exit path in plugin.sh. Add `_rr_write_result <artifact_dir> <verdict> <disposition> <reason>` helper (pattern from teardown/plugin.sh:52-61 and design/plugin.sh:56-61). Call it at: (1) missing state_file → verdict=error, disposition=broken; (2) missing out_json → verdict=error, disposition=broken; (3) router exhausted → verdict=pass, disposition=exhausted; (4) normal completion → verdict=pass, disposition=complete. The result file path is `$artifact_dir/review-report-result.json` — distinct from the advisory `review-report.json`. Run SPEC-a and SPEC-b to confirm all exit paths produce a conformant v2 result.

Produce a before/after golden diff to confirm the passing-run output is unchanged. Run `npm test` with all changes committed (so the mutation tier engages per CLAUDE.md). Confirm: (1) all new SPECs are green; (2) existing review-report tests still pass; (3) `grep -n 'extract_first_json_object' plugins/agent/review-report/lib/lenses.sh` returns no match (path construction assertion); (4) coverage floor not broken.

notes: PRIMARY OUTPUT ALREADY DECLARED: review-report/manifest.yaml already has `primary: true` on the `review_report` output (line 85). No change needed for that acceptance criterion — the issue asks us to record that fact. VALID_VERDICTS ALREADY []  with a lint comment — the plugin is advisory and emits no verdict through the verdict channel (it returns 0 always); the manifest already states `valid_verdicts: []` with an explicit claim comment. The issue says a verdict outside the declared set is a structural failure; because the plugin emits no verdict at all, the empty set is correct and no change is needed to that field specifically. RESULT FILE vs ADVISORY REPORT: the v2 result file (step-5) is the engine-readable contract artifact (result_contract/verdict/disposition/reason); the existing `review-report.json` is the advisory human-readable report. They are separate files. The output manifest should gain a new output entry for `review-report-result.json` with `required:true` (covered in step-5's manifest amendment). INPUTS: the issue's name-matched input migration (no `from:`, no path construction in code) appears already satisfied — the manifest uses `id:` only with no path or producer fields, and the plugin derives paths from state_dir rather than manifest paths. A grep assertion in step-6 will verify no hardcoded artifact paths remain. COORDINATE WITH #1719: review-summary comment count / verdict marker — the issue flags this but grants no scope to fix it here. Record as a known gap: this migration does not alter the PR-comment behaviour beyond existing fail-soft `gh pr comment`. CLEANUP HOOK: the plugin holds no live resources (no open sockets, no mounted volumes); the `cleanup` hook is legitimately absent. This must be recorded in the manifest with a comment, not implied by silence, per the issue's cleanup requirement (#1829). Add a `hooks:` comment or a `cleanup: ~` null entry in manifest.yaml in step-2. LENSES RUN IN SUBSHELLS: the budget-guidance injection in step-4 must write the budget into the per-lens prompt file (built sequentially before subshell launch) rather than relying on a subshell-visible variable, because subshells inherit env but not function calls on the hot path. The prompt file approach already used in _rr_fanout_lenses handles this naturally. GOLDEN DIFF: a golden file may not yet exist; step-6 may need to create it. The before-state must be captured from merge-base. If the golden dir has no existing snapshot this step produces the baseline rather than diffs it — record as a conditional.
